# Top Power BI and Microsoft Fabric analytics consultants in Brisbane

For operational reporting and data warehousing, I’d shortlist consultancies that can do more than build attractive Power BI dashboards. The strongest fit is a partner that can connect ERP and operational systems, create a reliable data warehouse or lakehouse, establish consistent KPI definitions, and deliver reporting that managers can use every day.

Based on current web research, these are the providers I’d investigate first. This is a **fit-based shortlist, not a definitive industry ranking**\: I’ve prioritised relevant technical capabilities, Brisbane presence, operational reporting experience, and evidence of Microsoft Fabric expertise.

## My recommended shortlist

![Strategix - Verosoft Partner — Verosoft](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/cpMLffNMjd7JvV_3POZ6DHgMvw4mDefTgsYwvgSP7IQ5PJiG2ysEhxT5K-Cng9HHgYzR6ssPFgtzES-qw9_Y2aeqIGVdZinNGVGzbRtFx8pdXdNvvVl6sUo4ubh6Uei8knBQA2Iv-EY8i94fDk3sJXhr7VtuPNsJ1bCKMiSw6ll3Kx3b0eIgc1aClPfcnlU4?purpose=fullsize)

(Strong operational fit)

**Best for\:** Operational dashboards, ERP reporting and management visibility.

Strategik focuses on extracting useful data from ERP and operational systems, improving Power BI reporting, and addressing gaps left by ERP implementations. It also offers Microsoft Fabric and Power Platform capabilities. Agile Insights advertises more than 150 Microsoft Fabric engagements, an all-certified consulting team, and an advanced Microsoft Analytics on Azure specialisation. It delivers nationally, with consultants across Queensland and other Australian states. [www.agile-insights.com.au](https://www.agile-insights.com.au/power-bi-consulting/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Why shortlist it\:** Particularly attractive if you have multiple business units, a growing Power BI estate, duplicated semantic models or enterprise governance requirements.

## 7\. Team 400

**Best for\:** Enterprise data warehousing, Fabric migrations and integrated analytics architecture.

Team 400 describes a Microsoft Fabric practice covering OneLake, lakehouse architecture, SQL data warehousing, real-time intelligence and Power BI, with senior specialists based in Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne. [team400.ai](https://team400.ai/microsoft-fabric-consultants?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Why shortlist it\:** A candidate for a larger data-platform programme where reporting, engineering and warehouse architecture need to be designed together.

Website: [team400.ai/microsoft-fabric-consultants](https://team400.ai/microsoft-fabric-consultants)

## Which consultants best match your requirements?

Here is how I would prioritise them for the two main parts of your project.

| Your priority | Start with | Reason |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Operational KPI dashboards and management reporting | **Strategik or Roar Data** | Strong focus on business processes, operational visibility and reducing manual reporting |
| Microsoft Fabric data warehouse and engineering | **Professional Advantage or Syonix** | Relevant capabilities across Fabric architecture, data pipelines and analytics foundations |
| Financial and operational reporting integrated with ERP | **Motta Consulting** | Published SAP-integrated reporting case study |
| Enterprise governance and Power BI at scale | **Agile Insights** | Focus on governed models, performance and enterprise Fabric adoption |
| Large-scale Fabric transformation | **Team 400** | Broad Fabric engineering and warehouse capabilities |


These are recommendations based on publicly described capabilities, not independently verified rankings of delivery quality.

## Three things I would verify before selecting a partner

1. **A comparable operational reporting project.** Ask for a reference involving your industry, source systems and reporting cadence.
2. **End-to-end delivery capability.** Confirm they can handle ingestion, warehouse or lakehouse design, data modelling, Power BI, security and production support—not just dashboards.
3. **Named consultants and commercial scope.** Ask who will personally deliver the work, which Microsoft Fabric certifications they hold, and whether the initial phase can be fixed-price.

For a Fabric-based solution, I would also ask them to demonstrate how they would reconcile source-system totals, define shared KPIs and manage data refresh failures.

## One question to narrow the shortlist

**What sort of business and operational data do you need to report on?**

1\. Business environment

Manufacturing, operations or supply chain

Construction, engineering or projects

Finance, professional services or corporate reporting

Government, health or another sector

---

2\. Main data sources

ERP (SAP, Dynamics, NetSuite or similar)

SQL databases, spreadsheets and operational applications

Existing data warehouse or Azure platform

Multiple systems, not yet consolidated

---

3\. What do you need delivered?

Power BI dashboards and reports only

Microsoft Fabric data warehouse and engineering

Both data warehouse and Power BI reporting

[Refine my shortlist]

With those details, I can narrow this to the **three most relevant Brisbane consultants** rather than a general list of Power BI providers.

## Three things I would verify before selecting a partner

1. **A comparable operational reporting project.** Ask for a reference involving your industry, source systems and reporting cadence.
2. **End-to-end delivery capability.** Confirm they can handle ingestion, warehouse or lakehouse design, data modelling, Power BI, security and production support—not just dashboards.
3. **Named consultants and commercial scope.** Ask who will personally deliver the work, which Microsoft Fabric certifications they hold, and whether the initial phase can be fixed-price.

For a Fabric-based solution, I would also ask them to demonstrate how they would reconcile source-system totals, define shared KPIs and manage data refresh failures.
